name: envcheck
problem: Apps crash because a local .env is missing variables that were added to .env.example, or code reads variables nobody documented.
solution: CLI that diffs .env against .env.example and scans source for env reads to flag undocumented variables.
learned: argparse exit-code design, regex-based source scanning, unittest with redirected stdio

name: csv2xlsx
problem: Excel guesses encoding and delimiter when opening CSVs, producing garbled accents, single-column data and mangled ids.
solution: CLI that detects encoding and delimiter and writes a real .xlsx using only the standard library.
learned: OOXML package layout, encoding fallback chain, delimiter detection by row consistency

name: sound-timer
problem: Practice timers count the whole session, so time spent not playing is counted as practice.
solution: Browser app that listens through the microphone and only runs the clock while it hears sound, bridging short rests.
learned: Web Audio API level metering, getUserMedia error handling, separating pure logic for Node tests, timer throttling in background tabs

name: bankcsv
problem: Bank CSV exports differ per bank (columns, dates, number formats, preamble lines), making multi-bank budgeting a manual clean-up.
solution: CLI that detects the layout, normalises to one CSV, applies keyword category rules and prints a monthly summary.
learned: Decimal money parsing across locales, header detection heuristics, inferring day-first vs month-first dates from a whole column

name: logfold
problem: Log lines that differ only by timestamp, id, IP or counter never match, so spotting what a log keeps repeating needs hand-written sed before sort | uniq -c.
solution: Go CLI that normalises variable parts into placeholders, groups matching lines anywhere in the input and prints counted patterns.
learned: RE2 has no lookahead so rule order and word boundaries matter; testing a CLI by making main a run(args, stdin, stdout, stderr) function

name: tzquick
problem: Converting a time between zones means a converter site with dropdowns or error-prone mental offset maths; people asked for a tool that takes a phrase like 'today 17:00 Pacific in UTC'.
solution: Static browser page that parses a plain phrase and converts it with built-in Intl time zone data, flagging DST gaps, repeated hours and ambiguous abbreviations.
learned: Turning wall-clock time into an instant with Intl needs an offset round-trip check to detect DST gaps and repeats; keeping parsing in a DOM-free module made it testable under node:test

name: dirdiff
problem: After a backup, restore or reorganisation there is no quick way to tell whether two folders really match; name and timestamp comparison misses corruption and reports renames as a delete plus a new file.
solution: Rust CLI that compares two folders by SHA-256 content and classifies files as identical, changed, moved or renamed, or only on one side, with exit codes for scripting.
learned: Implementing SHA-256 including padding edge cases, avoiding needless hashing by comparing sizes first, and testing a Rust binary through CARGO_BIN_EXE

name: drivecat
problem: Old external disks and DVDs sit in a drawer and nobody remembers which one holds a file; people asked for a tool that indexes them so they can be searched while unplugged.
solution: Python CLI that catalogs file names, sizes and dates into SQLite, then searches, browses, sizes and finds same-name duplicates across disks offline.
learned: A leaked SQLite connection on a corrupt file locks it on Windows, so close on every failure path; storing relative posix paths keeps catalogs portable between operating systems

name: srtfix
problem: Downloaded SRT subtitles start early or late or drift because of a frame-rate mismatch, and player delay settings are not saved into the file.
solution: Node CLI that shifts, stretches or two-point syncs SRT timings, validates cues and renumbers the file.
learned: Linear two-point time mapping for drift, tolerant SRT parsing (BOM, CRLF, missing indexes), node:test for a zero-dependency CLI

name: awscron
problem: AWS EventBridge cron differs from Unix cron (six fields, year, Sunday=1, one of day-of-month/day-of-week must be ?), and rules are only rejected with a generic error at deploy time.
solution: Node CLI that validates cron() and rate() expressions with specific error messages and prints the next run times in UTC.
learned: AWS cron edge rules (L, W, nL, n#m), computing nearest-weekday without leaving the month, and that node --test needs a glob on Windows

name: cidrplan
problem: Network allocations kept in wikis and spreadsheets overlap by accident, and working out what is still free means manual binary arithmetic.
solution: Go CLI that reads a text list of IPv4 CIDRs, reports overlaps and duplicates, lists free space inside a parent range and finds the next aligned free block.
learned: Splitting an address range into minimal aligned CIDRs, merging overlapping intervals, uint32 edge cases at the top of the IPv4 space, net/netip strict prefix parsing

name: rangespec
problem: Reports and queries need exact date ranges, and working out phrases like 'last full quarter' or '4 weeks ago to 2 weeks from now' by hand leads to off-by-one errors; people asked for a parser for simple, relative and to-style ranges.
solution: Python CLI and importable parser that resolves plain-English date ranges against a fixed today and prints inclusive start and end dates as text, ISO, JSON, a SQL condition or a day list.
learned: Calendar arithmetic with month-end clamping, why a to-style splitter must handle phrases like 'year to date' before splitting, and making the resolver a pure function of an explicit today so tests are deterministic

name: permcheck
problem: Secret files such as .env, cloud credentials and registry tokens are often left readable by other users on the machine; only ssh complains about loose key permissions.
solution: Rust CLI that finds secret-looking files by name, reports modes that expose them to group or others, and optionally strips those bits.
learned: Unix mode-bit arithmetic, testing real chmod behaviour in temp folders (default umask makes directories 0755), and why --fix should only ever remove bits

name: portname
problem: Files copied to Windows, macOS or OneDrive fail on names that were fine elsewhere: reserved names like CON, illegal characters, trailing dots, case-only duplicates and paths over 260 characters. Sync clients report one file at a time.
solution: TypeScript CLI for Deno that lists every problem name in a folder or a stdin path list for chosen targets, explains why and suggests a safe replacement, without touching any file.
learned: Windows matches device names on the part before the first dot, name length is UTF-16 units on Windows but UTF-8 bytes on macOS, and String.normalize makes macOS normalization collisions testable; reporting each bad parent folder once keeps output readable

name: jsonshape
problem: Unfamiliar JSON or NDJSON dumps are hard to understand before writing code: which keys are optional, which have mixed types, what ranges values take.
solution: Python CLI that prints one line per key path with types, presence rate, numeric ranges, lengths and an example.
learned: Aggregating heterogeneous records into per-path statistics; auto-detecting JSON vs NDJSON; testing a CLI via an injectable main

name: hexfind
problem: Hex editors and grep can find a magic number but not a header followed by a field with a sensible value, so most chance hits of the magic bytes have to be checked by hand; Hacker News users asked for fuzzy search over header fields.
solution: Python CLI that matches patterns of literal bytes, wildcards and typed integer fields with constraints, and prints each match offset with the decoded field values.
learned: Using mmap for scanning with bytes.find to jump to the first literal, struct format codes for endianness and sign, and keeping a pattern parser strict so typos fail with a clear message

name: seqgap
problem: Accountants and auditors need to know whether invoice, credit note or cheque numbers have holes or duplicates, and checking by hand across several mixed series is slow and error-prone.
solution: Go CLI that groups identifiers into series by prefix and suffix and reports missing ranges, duplicates, out-of-order entries and inconsistent padding from a list or a CSV column.
learned: Splitting identifiers around the last digit run to define a series, reporting gaps as ranges so huge gaps stay cheap, and that CSV line numbers should include the header row to match spreadsheet rows

name: headlinecheck
problem: People want a clickbait headline filter, but existing ones target video thumbnails or give a verdict with no reason.
solution: Rule-based scorer with readable reasons, shipped as a Manifest V3 extension that dims or labels headlines and as a CLI.
learned: Manifest V3 content scripts and storage, sharing one UMD module between extension, CLI and tests, MutationObserver debouncing, tuning heuristic offsets

name: branchsweep
problem: git branch --merged misses branches merged by squash or rebase, so local branches pile up and cleanup relies on risky one-liners.
solution: CLI that classifies local branches (merged, squash-merged via git cherry, upstream gone, stale) and deletes only with explicit flags.
learned: Patch-id based merge detection with git cherry, for-each-ref formats, building throwaway git repos for tests

name: csv2ics
problem: Getting a spreadsheet timetable or event list into a calendar means Google's strict CSV import (Google only, US dates, no repeats), Outlook's separate wizard, or a one-off script.
solution: Dependency-free Node CLI and in-browser page that map loose CSV headers to RFC 5545 events, with time zones, all-day and multi-day events, weekly/monthly repeats and per-row error reports.
learned: RFC 5545 escaping, line folding by octets and RRULE UNTIL rules, wall-time to UTC conversion with Intl.DateTimeFormat across DST gaps and overlaps, sharing one ES module between CLI and browser

name: cronlint
problem: Cron jobs that work in a terminal fail silently under cron because of its minimal PATH, unescaped % characters, relative paths, sh-only syntax and unread mail output.
solution: Go CLI that lints crontab files for schedule errors and these environment pitfalls, with optional on-disk command lookup against cron's PATH.
learned: Cron semantics (day-of-month OR day-of-week, percent handling, default PATH and shell), range/step field parsing, testing filesystem lookups with temp dirs and t.Setenv

name: invoiceage
problem: Freelancers tracking invoices in a spreadsheet have no quick way to see who is overdue and by how long, and reminder emails keep getting put off.
solution: CLI that reads an invoice CSV, prints an aging report with per-client overdue totals and drafts reminders whose tone depends on how late each invoice is.
learned: Decimal money handling, tolerant CSV header mapping, exit codes that distinguish overdue from bad input

name: contrastfix
problem: Checking a palette's colour pairs against WCAG one at a time is slow, and failing pairs get fixed by trial and error.
solution: Rust CLI that checks many pairs at once and suggests the nearest foreground colour, same hue, that passes AA or AAA.
learned: WCAG luminance maths, HSL round-trips and rounding, testing a Rust binary with CARGO_BIN_EXE

name: settleup
problem: Shared expenses between housemates or trip groups end up in spreadsheets or apps that need accounts; people want a local, scriptable way to see who owes whom.
solution: Node CLI that reads a plain text expense list (equal, weighted or exact splits), computes balances in integer cents and prints the fewest payments that settle everyone.
learned: Largest remainder rounding, bitmask DP to partition balances into zero-sum groups, keeping money as integer cents

name: spflint
problem: SPF and DMARC records fail silently when they have a typo, a second SPF record or more than 10 DNS lookups, and online checkers only work after the record is published.
solution: Offline Python CLI that lints SPF and DMARC records, counts DNS lookups (optionally expanding includes from a local JSON file) and reports errors and warnings with exit codes.
learned: SPF term grammar and the 10-lookup limit, recursive include expansion with loop detection, designing a lint CLI with separate error and warning severities

name: linesets
problem: Comparing lists of lines across files is clumsy: comm needs sorted input and exactly two files, uniq -d miscounts repeats within a file, and case or whitespace differences hide matches.
solution: Go CLI that treats each file as a set of lines and prints union, common, only, diff or at-least-k results, with case/whitespace normalisation and per-line file counts.
learned: Go flag package stops at the first positional argument so interleaved flags need a parse loop; set semantics with duplicates inside a file; testing a CLI through a run() function with injected streams

name: todoage
problem: TODO and FIXME comments pile up in a codebase and grep cannot say which ones are years old and need a decision.
solution: Rust CLI that finds tagged comments, uses git blame to age each line, and lists them oldest first with filters, JSON output and a CI-friendly exit code.
learned: Parsing git blame --porcelain (headers only repeat per commit); building backdated test repos with GIT_AUTHOR_DATE; avoiding byte-index panics on Unicode lines

name: gradeneed
problem: Students with weighted grading and drop-lowest rules have to redo the arithmetic by hand to learn what they need on the final, and online calculators are limited or ad-heavy.
solution: Dependency-free JavaScript module with a CLI and a static offline page that reads a small text spec and reports the average needed on pending work for each target grade.
learned: Designing a tiny line-based spec format with line-numbered errors; one module shared between Node and the browser; handling secured and out-of-reach cases explicitly

name: mdrefs
problem: Renamed files and reworded headings leave dead relative links and #anchors in Markdown docs that most link checkers do not catch.
solution: Offline Python CLI that verifies local link targets and GitHub-style heading anchors, including reference-style links and code-fence skipping.
learned: GitHub heading slug rules, duplicate-heading suffixes, tokenising Markdown links without a parser, skipping code fences

name: datename
problem: Photos, screenshots and downloads have inconsistent names that do not sort by date, and EXIF-only renamers skip files with no EXIF data.
solution: Go CLI that renames files by date taken from EXIF, then a date in the file name, then modified time, with dry run by default and collision handling.
learned: Hand-parsing JPEG segments and TIFF IFDs with bounds checks, regex limits without lookaround in Go, safe batch renames with collision suffixes

name: robotscheck
problem: Checking whether a URL is blocked by robots.txt means pasting into an online tester or using parsers that apply the first matching rule instead of the most specific one.
solution: Offline Rust CLI that applies RFC 9309 matching (longest rule wins, Allow wins ties, * and $ wildcards, user-agent group selection) and can explain which rule decided each URL.
learned: Iterative wildcard matching with backtracking, RFC 9309 precedence rules, and how group merging and stacked user-agent lines change which rules apply

name: plainwrite
problem: Readability checkers are usually online services with logins or uploads; people want a free local way to check whether writing is plain and which sentences cause trouble.
solution: Dependency-free JavaScript module with a CLI and an offline HTML page that reports reading ease, grade level and flags long, passive, filler and repeated-word sentences.
learned: Syllable counting by regex is only approximate; sharing one module between Node and the browser needs a guarded module.exports; testing a CLI through an injected run(args, stdin, out, err, readFile)
